items.stem: A hockey puck slides at constant velocity across frictionless ice. What is the net force on it?

options.text: Zero, because constant velocity means no acceleration
options.rationale: Correct: Newton's first and second laws require zero net force when acceleration is zero.

options.text: A forward force equal to its weight
options.rationale: No forward force is needed to maintain constant velocity.

options.text: A force in the direction of motion that decreases over time
options.rationale: Constant velocity means zero acceleration and therefore zero net force.
Vertical forces balance; the net force is zero in all directions.

items.explanation: Correct: Newton's first and second laws require zero net force when acceleration is zero.

items.stem: Which TWO quantities are always conserved for an isolated system of colliding particles, regardless of whether the collision is elastic or inelastic? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: momentum is conserved for an isolated system in every collision.
Mechanical energy is conserved only in elastic collisions.
Correct: mass is conserved in classical collisions.
Kinetic energy is lost to heat and deformation in inelastic collisions.

items.explanation: Correct: momentum is conserved for an isolated system in every collision.

items.stem: A solid disk and a hoop of equal mass and radius are released from rest down the same incline. Which reaches the bottom first and why?

options.text: The disk, because it has a smaller moment of inertia so more energy goes into translation
options.rationale: Correct: a smaller moment of inertia leaves more energy for translational kinetic energy.

options.text: The hoop, because its mass is at the rim
options.rationale: The hoop's larger moment of inertia slows its translation.

options.text: They tie, because mass and radius are equal
options.rationale: Moment of inertia differs by shape even at equal mass and radius.

options.text: The hoop, because it rolls without slipping
options.rationale: Both roll without slipping; the difference is the moment of inertia.

items.explanation: Correct: a smaller moment of inertia leaves more energy for translational kinetic energy.
